name: 74HCT193D,653
title: 74HC193; 74HCT193: presettable synchronous 4-bit binary up/down counter
summary: A 4-bit binary counter with one clock for counting up (CPU) and another for counting down (CPD); all four outputs move together on the rising edge of whichever clock is pulsed while the other is held HIGH. MR clears the count and PL loads D0 to D3 at once, both without a clock. Active-LOW carry (TCU) and borrow (TCD) outputs repeat the clock at the ends of the count, so counters chain with no extra gates. The 74HC193 runs from 2.0 V to 6.0 V with CMOS input levels and the 74HCT193 from 4.5 V to 5.5 V with TTL input levels.
key_figures: Propagation delay CPU, CPD to Qn
23 ns typ, 43 ns max at VCC = 4.5 V, 25 °C

circuits.title: Cascaded up/down counter with parallel load
circuits.description: Two counters chained into one 8-bit up/down counter. The first counter takes the up and down clocks; its TCU and TCD outputs clock CPU and CPD of the second, so the second advances once each time the first rolls past 15 or below 0. The load and reset lines go to both counters together, presetting all eight bits from the data inputs or clearing them, and the second counter's TCU and TCD are the carry and borrow outputs.

circuits.title: Test circuit for switching times
circuits.description: A pulse generator, with a resistor to ground matching its output impedance, drives the input of the device under test. The output sees a load capacitor to ground and a load resistor that runs to a switch able to reach VCC, ground or nothing; for tPHL and tPLH the switch stays open.

where.CPD: power dissipation capacitance, pF (24 pF typ 74HC193, 26 pF typ 74HCT193)
where.CL: load capacitance on an output, pF

operation.text: Pulsing CPU with CPD held HIGH counts up; pulsing CPD with CPU held HIGH counts down. Q0 to Q3 change together on the clock's LOW-to-HIGH edge. The clock not in use is held HIGH for predictable counting.
MR HIGH forces Q0 to Q3 LOW at any moment, overriding both clocks and blocking the parallel load. Reset wins over loading, the data lines and counting.
While PL is LOW (and MR is LOW) the levels on D0 to D3 appear on Q0 to Q3 whatever the clocks are doing. This presets the counter to any value.

operation.topic: First edge after reset or load
operation.text: A clock input that stays LOW through a reset or load and beyond it is not ignored: its following LOW-to-HIGH edge is taken as a genuine clock and steps the counter.

TCU and TCD sit HIGH. At a count of 15, the falling edge of CPU takes TCU LOW and it stays LOW until CPU rises again, so TCU is a copy of the up clock. At a count of 0, TCD does the same with CPD. These copies serve as the clocks of the next counter in a chain.
A chain built by feeding TCU and TCD into the next stage's CPU and CPD needs no extra logic, but it is not fully synchronous: each stage adds its own small delay.

Clear to zero, load thirteen, count up through 14, 15 (TCU pulses), 0, 1, 2, then count down through 1, 0 (TCD pulses), 15, 14, 13. During counting up CPD is held HIGH, and during counting down CPU is held HIGH.
The inputs have clamp diodes, so a series current-limiting resistor lets an input be driven from a voltage higher than VCC.
74HC193 inputs switch at CMOS levels; 74HCT193 inputs switch at TTL levels.
On the 74HCT193 an input held at VCC - 2.1 V adds supply current ΔICC: at 25 °C up to 126 µA for a Dn input, 504 µA for CPU or CPD, 234 µA for PL and 378 µA for MR.
Meets JESD8C (2.7 V to 3.6 V) and JESD7A (2.0 V to 6.0 V). Specified over -40 °C to +85 °C and -40 °C to +125 °C.
